views.name: sales_with_time_product_customer_channel_promo
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  sales.prod_id AS prod_id,
  sales.cust_id AS cust_id,
  sales.time_id AS time_id,
  sales.channel_id AS channel_id,
  sales.promo_id AS promo_id,
  sales.quantity_sold AS quantity_sold,
  sales.amount_sold AS amount_sold,
  times.day_name AS day_name,
  times.calendar_month_desc AS calendar_month_desc,
  times.calendar_year AS calendar_year,
  products.prod_name AS prod_name,
  products.prod_category AS prod_category,
  products.prod_subcategory AS prod_subcategory,
  products.prod_list_price AS prod_list_price,
  customers.cust_first_name AS cust_first_name,
  customers.cust_last_name AS cust_last_name,
  customers.cust_gender AS cust_gender,
  customers.country_id AS country_id,
  channels.channel_desc AS channel_desc,
  promotions.promo_name AS promo_name,
  promotions.promo_category AS promo_category
FROM sales
LEFT JOIN times ON sales.time_id = times.time_id
LEFT JOIN products ON sales.prod_id = products.prod_id
LEFT JOIN customers ON sales.cust_id = customers.cust_id
LEFT JOIN channels ON sales.channel_id = channels.channel_id
LEFT JOIN promotions ON sales.promo_id = promotions.promo_id

params.description: A row-level denormalized sales view at the grain of (prod_id, cust_id, time_id, channel_id, promo_id) that combines sales measures with time, product, customer, channel and promotion attributes.
params.when_to_use: Querying or slicing sales measures (quantity_sold, amount_sold) by any combination of product, customer, time, channel, or promotion attributes (for example: sales by product category by month, revenue by promotion by channel, sales to customers by gender and product subcategory). | Building higher-level aggregations (daily/monthly/yearly totals) or filtered reports that start from detailed sales rows. | Joining to other dimension tables that are one-row-per-key (e.g., canonical product or customer current-version views) without risk of duplicating measures. | Serving as the base for further aggregations, window calculations, or to feed downstream joins when preserved row-level sales measures are required.
params.output_schema: prod_id: product business key from sales.prod_id (source: sales.prod_id) | cust_id: customer business key from sales.cust_id (source: sales.cust_id) | time_id: time key from sales.time_id (source: sales.time_id) | channel_id: channel key from sales.channel_id (source: sales.channel_id) | promo_id: promotion key from sales.promo_id (source: sales.promo_id) | quantity_sold: sold quantity measure copied from sales.quantity_sold (source: sales.quantity_sold) | amount_sold: sold revenue/amount measure copied from sales.amount_sold (source: sales.amount_sold) | day_name: day name attribute from times.day_name joined by sales.time_id = times.time_id (source: times.day_name) | calendar_month_desc: month label from times.calendar_month_desc joined by sales.time_id = times.time_id (source: times.calendar_month_desc) | calendar_year: year number from times.calendar_year joined by sales.time_id = times.time_id (source: times.calendar_year) | prod_name: product name attribute from products.prod_name joined by sales.prod_id = products.prod_id (source: products.prod_name) | prod_category: product category attribute from products.prod_category joined by sales.prod_id = products.prod_id (source: products.prod_category) | prod_subcategory: product subcategory attribute from products.prod_subcategory joined by sales.prod_id = products.prod_id (source: products.prod_subcategory) | prod_list_price: product list price attribute from products.prod_list_price joined by sales.prod_id = products.prod_id (source: products.prod_list_price) | cust_first_name: customer first name attribute from customers.cust_first_name joined by sales.cust_id = customers.cust_first_name (source: customers.cust_first_name) | cust_last_name: customer last name attribute from customers.cust_last_name joined by sales.cust_id = customers.cust_last_name (source: customers.cust_last_name) | cust_gender: customer gender attribute from customers.cust_gender joined by sales.cust_id = customers.cust_id (source: customers.cust_gender) | country_id: customer country key from customers.country_id joined by sales.cust_id = customers.cust_id (source: customers.country_id) | channel_desc: channel description attribute from channels.channel_desc joined by sales.channel_id = channels.channel_id (source: channels.channel_desc) | promo_name: promotion name attribute from promotions.promo_name joined by sales.promo_id = promotions.promo_id (source: promotions.promo_name) | promo_category: promotion category attribute from promotions.promo_category joined by sales.promo_id = promotions.promo_id (source: promotions.promo_category)
params.grounded_columns: sales.prod_id | sales.cust_id | sales.time_id | sales.channel_id | sales.promo_id | sales.quantity_sold | sales.amount_sold | times.time_id | times.day_name | times.calendar_month_desc | times.calendar_year | products.prod_id | products.prod_name | products.prod_category | products.prod_subcategory | products.prod_list_price | customers.cust_id | customers.cust_first_name | customers.cust_last_name | customers.cust_gender | customers.country_id | channels.channel_id | channels.channel_desc | promotions.promo_id | promotions.promo_name | promotions.promo_category
params.metric: quantity_sold = direct measure, copied from sales.quantity_sold (no aggregation in this view). | amount_sold = direct monetary measure, copied from sales.amount_sold (no aggregation in this view).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to product_current_versions on prod_id — safe because product_current_versions(RANK) should be one-row-per-prod_id (current version). Joining will not multiply sales measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to customer_current_versions on cust_id — safe because customer_current_versions(RANK) should be one-row-per-cust_id (current version). Joining will not multiply sales measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to times (or any time-dimension that is one-row-per-time_id) on time_id — safe because times is keyed by time_id, preserving row uniqueness. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to channels on channel_id — safe if channels is one-row-per-channel_id; joining will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to promotions on promo_id — safe if promotions is one-row-per-promo_id; joining will not duplicate measures. | do NOT join without aggregation to sibling AGG views that are many-to-one to this view's grain (for example, joining to monthly_sales_agg_by_product_channel_promo directly on (prod_id, calendar_month_desc, channel_id, promo_id) is allowed only if the AGG is one-row-per-(prod,month,channel,promo). If that AGG is one-row-per-(prod,month,channel,promo) it is safe; verify its grain before joining.) | do NOT join this view directly to any table or view that is one-to-many from the sales grain (for example, a table of multiple customer addresses, multiple product_versions without a single-current filter, or any detailed promotion-event-log with multiple rows per promo_id) because such joins will multiply quantity_sold and amount_sold. Instead, either (a) aggregate that detail to one row per join key before joining, or (b) join to a curated one-row-per-key dimension (e.g., product_current_versions, customer_current_versions). | when composing aggregations: SUM(quantity_sold) and SUM(amount_sold) over this view produce correct totals at any coarser grain built by grouping on subsets of {prod_id, cust_id, time_id, channel_id, promo_id} or their attributes (e.g., prod_category, calendar_month_desc). | when joining to windowed or running-total views (e.g., sales_running_total_by_product_month), ensure the other view's grain aligns (one-row-per-prod+month) or pre-aggregate/re-key so that rows are not duplicated; prefer joining aggregated monthly keys (prod_id + calendar_month_desc) and avoid joining raw event logs that have multiple rows per key.

views.description: Denormalized sales fact joined to core dimensions (times, products, customers, channels, promotions). Use this when you need descriptive attributes alongside sales measures for filtering, grouping, or further aggregation. Preserves original keys for downstream joins. | Use for: Sales by product/category/month/year; Customer-level purchase history with product and promotion context; Channel or promotion effectiveness analysis; Filtering sales by product attributes or customer demographics

views.name: product_current_versions
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  prod_id AS prod_id,
  prod_name AS prod_name,
  prod_desc AS prod_desc,
  prod_subcategory AS prod_subcategory,
  prod_subcategory_id AS prod_subcategory_id,
  prod_subcategory_desc AS prod_subcategory_desc,
  prod_category AS prod_category,
  prod_category_id AS prod_category_id,
  prod_category_desc AS prod_category_desc,
  prod_weight_class AS prod_weight_class,
  prod_unit_of_measure AS prod_unit_of_measure,
  prod_pack_size AS prod_pack_size,
  supplier_id AS supplier_id,
  prod_status AS prod_status,
  prod_list_price AS prod_list_price,
  prod_min_price AS prod_min_price,
  prod_eff_from AS prod_eff_from,
  prod_eff_to AS prod_eff_to,
  prod_valid AS prod_valid,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY prod_id ORDER BY CASE WHEN prod_valid = 'A' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, prod_eff_from DESC NULLS LAST) AS version_rank
FROM products

params.description: Provides the current and historical ranked versions per product (one row per product-version rank), highlighting the active version first so callers can pick current product attributes.
params.when_to_use: Get the current product attributes (pick version_rank = 1) including pricing, supplier, categorization and validity window. | Analyze product version history ordered by effective-from date and active flag (e.g., audit/report of changes over time). | Compose with sales or cost aggregates by prod_id to attribute transactions to the applicable product version (join on prod_id and filter by prod_eff_from/prod_eff_to or use version_rank = 1). | Enrich transactional or aggregated facts with product descriptive attributes and current list/min prices.
params.output_schema: prod_id: product identifier, derived directly from products.prod_id | prod_name: product name/label, derived directly from products.prod_name | prod_desc: product description, derived directly from products.prod_desc | prod_subcategory: subcategory name for the product, derived directly from products.prod_subcategory | prod_subcategory_id: subcategory identifier, derived directly from products.prod_subcategory_id | prod_subcategory_desc: subcategory description, derived directly from products.prod_subcategory_desc | prod_category: category name for the product, derived directly from products.prod_category | prod_category_id: category identifier, derived directly from products.prod_category_id | prod_category_desc: category description, derived directly from products.prod_category_desc | prod_weight_class: product weight class, derived directly from products.prod_weight_class | prod_unit_of_measure: product unit of measure, derived directly from products.prod_unit_of_measure | prod_pack_size: package size, derived directly from products.prod_pack_size | supplier_id: supplier identifier for the product, derived directly from products.supplier_id | prod_status: status code (e.g., A=active), derived directly from products.prod_status | prod_list_price: list price of the product version, derived directly from products.prod_list_price | prod_min_price: minimum allowed price for the product version, derived directly from products.prod_min_price | prod_eff_from: version effective-from timestamp/date, derived directly from products.prod_eff_from | prod_eff_to: version effective-to timestamp/date, derived directly from products.prod_eff_to | prod_valid: flag/indicator of validity (e.g., 'A' for active), derived directly from products.prod_valid | version_rank: integer rank assigned per prod_id (ROW_NUMBER) ordering active versions first then by prod_eff_from desc, computed in the view
params.grounded_columns: products.prod_id | products.prod_name | products.prod_desc | products.prod_subcategory | products.prod_subcategory_id | products.prod_subcategory_desc | products.prod_category | products.prod_category_id | products.prod_category_desc | products.prod_weight_class | products.prod_unit_of_measure | products.prod_pack_size | products.supplier_id | products.prod_status | products.prod_list_price | products.prod_min_price | products.prod_eff_from | products.prod_eff_to | products.prod_valid
params.metric: version_rank = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY products.prod_id ORDER BY CASE WHEN products.prod_valid = 'A' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, products.prod_eff_from DESC NULLS LAST)  -- non-aggregated window rank per prod_id, computed in SQL
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to fact or aggregate views on prod_id when those facts are at a coarser grain (one row per transaction, per month, etc.) — safe because product_current_versions has one row per product-version (and if you filter to version_rank = 1 it is one row per prod_id) so joining on prod_id will not duplicate product-level attributes. | Join to sales_with_time_product_customer_channel_promo on prod_id is safe when you filter this view to version_rank = 1 (one row per prod_id). If you join without filtering to version_rank = 1, multiple version rows per prod_id will multiply fact rows. | Join to product_costs_by_month or monthly_sales_agg_by_product_channel_promo on prod_id and the appropriate month is safe only when you (a) filter product_current_versions to a single version row per prod_id (e.g., version_rank = 1) or (b) aggregate the joined result by the desired grain (e.g., SUM by month) to avoid duplicating measures. | Do NOT naively join this view to any one-to-many dimension (e.g., a product -> many images table, product -> many tags) without either (a) reducing that one-to-many side to one row per prod_id (for example by choosing a primary image) or (b) re-aggregating measures after the join. Such joins will duplicate product_current_versions rows and thus duplicate any measures derived from it. | When composing with time-aware facts: to map a transaction to the correct product version, join on prod_id AND filter facts.event_time between prod_eff_from (inclusive) and prod_eff_to (exclusive/null-as-infinite) — this avoids incorrectly attributing facts to the wrong version and prevents multiplying versions arbitrarily. | When joining to sibling RANK views (e.g., customer_current_versions), the join is safe if both sides are filtered to their respective '_rank = 1' (one-row-per-entity). If you need multiple versions from either side, first decide the composition semantics and re-aggregate measures to the target grain.

views.description: Choose the current/active product row per prod_id using prod_eff_from and prod_valid. Exposes a version_rank so downstream queries can select the latest record per product. Use when you need canonical current product attributes. | Use for: Get the current active product attributes for reporting; Join canonical product row to sales or costs; Identify historical vs current product records

views.name: customer_current_versions
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cust_id AS cust_id,
  cust_first_name AS cust_first_name,
  cust_last_name AS cust_last_name,
  cust_gender AS cust_gender,
  cust_year_of_birth AS cust_year_of_birth,
  cust_marital_status AS cust_marital_status,
  cust_street_address AS cust_street_address,
  cust_postal_code AS cust_postal_code,
  cust_city AS cust_city,
  cust_city_id AS cust_city_id,
  cust_state_province AS cust_state_province,
  cust_state_province_id AS cust_state_province_id,
  country_id AS country_id,
  cust_main_phone_number AS cust_main_phone_number,
  cust_income_level AS cust_income_level,
  cust_credit_limit AS cust_credit_limit,
  cust_email AS cust_email,
  cust_eff_from AS cust_eff_from,
  cust_eff_to AS cust_eff_to,
  cust_valid AS cust_valid,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY cust_id ORDER BY CASE WHEN cust_valid = 'A' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, cust_eff_from DESC NULLS LAST) AS version_rank
FROM customers

params.description: Provides the current (most relevant) version(s) of each customer record with a deterministic version rank to identify the effective row per customer.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve the current active customer attributes for reporting, joining to sales or other fact tables to attribute transactions to the customer's current profile. | Filter customers by current attributes (city, state, income level, validity) while ensuring one row per customer-version_rank. | Compose aggregations by customer (counts, distinct customers) using the current customer snapshot as the base dimension. | Build demographic breakdowns (by gender, age cohort, city, state, country) using current values without duplicating customer rows.
params.output_schema: cust_id: Customer surrogate/key — derived directly from customers.cust_id | cust_first_name: Customer given name — derived directly from customers.cust_first_name | cust_last_name: Customer family name — derived directly from customers.cust_last_name | cust_gender: Customer gender code/value — derived directly from customers.cust_gender | cust_year_of_birth: Year of birth (int) — derived directly from customers.cust_year_of_birth | cust_marital_status: Marital status code/value — derived directly from customers.cust_marital_status | cust_street_address: Street address text — derived directly from customers.cust_street_address | cust_postal_code: Postal / ZIP code — derived directly from customers.cust_postal_code | cust_city: City name text — derived directly from customers.cust_city | cust_city_id: City identifier — derived directly from customers.cust_city_id | cust_state_province: State / province name — derived directly from customers.cust_state_province | cust_state_province_id: State / province identifier — derived directly from customers.cust_state_province_id | country_id: Country identifier — derived directly from customers.country_id | cust_main_phone_number: Primary phone number — derived directly from customers.cust_main_phone_number | cust_income_level: Income level category/value — derived directly from customers.cust_income_level | cust_credit_limit: Credit limit numeric — derived directly from customers.cust_credit_limit | cust_email: Email address — derived directly from customers.cust_email | cust_eff_from: Effective-from timestamp/date for this customer row — derived directly from customers.cust_eff_from | cust_eff_to: Effective-to timestamp/date for this customer row — derived directly from customers.cust_eff_to | cust_valid: Validity flag (e.g., 'A' for active) — derived directly from customers.cust_valid | version_rank: Row number rank within each cust_id that orders preferred/current rows first — defined as ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY cust_id ORDER BY CASE WHEN cust_valid = 'A' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, cust_eff_from DESC NULLS LAST)
params.grounded_columns: customers.cust_id | customers.cust_first_name | customers.cust_last_name | customers.cust_gender | customers.cust_year_of_birth | customers.cust_marital_status | customers.cust_street_address | customers.cust_postal_code | customers.cust_city | customers.cust_city_id | customers.cust_state_province | customers.cust_state_province_id | customers.country_id | customers.cust_main_phone_number | customers.cust_income_level | customers.cust_credit_limit | customers.cust_email | customers.cust_eff_from | customers.cust_eff_to | customers.cust_valid
params.metric: version_rank = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customers.cust_id ORDER BY CASE WHEN customers.cust_valid = 'A' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, customers.cust_eff_from DESC NULLS LAST)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to fact tables (e.g., sales_with_time_product_customer_channel_promo) on cust_id — safe because this view is one row per (cust_id, version_rank) and does not aggregate measures; joining sales fact -> this view will not duplicate sales rows (facts remain grain of the fact) and each sale will match to at most one current customer row if you restrict to version_rank = 1. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension-like current-version views such as product_current_versions on their key(s) — safe when both sides are one-row-per-key (no multiplication of measures). | do NOT join this view directly to one-to-many child tables (e.g., a customer_addresses_history or multiple customer_phones table with many rows per cust_id) without either (a) aggregating the child to one row per cust_id or (b) re-aggregating after the join. Direct joins to such one-to-many details will multiply this view's rows and any downstream counts/metrics computed over customers. | do NOT join to sibling aggregate views that are at a finer grain than this view without aligning grain. For example, joining to a per-order or per-sale aggregate (monthly_sales_agg_by_product_channel_promo) without grouping by cust_id on the fact side or restricting to a single customer-level row can create duplication or incorrect aggregations. | When composing metrics: to compute customer-level metrics (e.g., number of customers by city), use this view restricted to version_rank = 1 to get exactly one row per customer, then aggregate. If you need historical customer versions, include version_rank in GROUP BY to preserve distinct versions. | If joining to currency_monthly_rates or product_costs_by_month (time-series or month-level tables), join on cust_eff_from / cust_eff_to carefully: these are effective-date attributes — ensure you either (a) join on a specific transaction date from the fact (not the customer eff_from) or (b) perform a range join using the fact event date to avoid duplication and to ground rates to the correct month.

views.description: Select a current/primary customer record per cust_id using cust_eff_from and cust_valid. Exposes version_rank so consumers can pick the latest active customer row. Useful for joining customer demographics to facts. | Use for: Attach current customer attributes to sales; Analyze customer lifetime metrics using canonical customer row; Resolve slowly-changing customer dimension for reporting

views.name: monthly_sales_agg_by_product_channel_promo
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  prod_id AS prod_id,
  channel_id AS channel_id,
  promo_id AS promo_id,
  calendar_month_desc AS calendar_month_desc,
  calendar_year AS calendar_year,
  SUM(quantity_sold) AS quantity_total,
  SUM(amount_sold) AS amount_total
FROM sales
LEFT JOIN times ON sales.time_id = times.time_id
GROUP BY prod_id, channel_id, promo_id, calendar_month_desc, calendar_year

params.description: Monthly totals of quantity and sales amount for each product × channel × promotion (calendar month and year).
params.when_to_use: Get monthly sales totals (quantity and amount) for a specific product, channel, or promo. | Compare product × channel × promo performance across calendar months or years. | Use as a pre-aggregated building block when composing higher-level reports (e.g., product-month trends, channel-level rollups, promo effectiveness) without re-scanning raw sales.
params.output_schema: prod_id: product identifier — derived from sales.prod_id (grouping key propagated from sales). | channel_id: channel identifier — derived from sales.channel_id (grouping key propagated from sales). | promo_id: promotion identifier — derived from sales.promo_id (grouping key propagated from sales). | calendar_month_desc: human-readable month (e.g., 'Jan 2024') — derived from times.calendar_month_desc (joined from times.time_id and grouped). | calendar_year: year integer (e.g., 2024) — derived from times.calendar_year (joined from times.time_id and grouped). | quantity_total: total quantity sold in that prod × channel × promo × month — derived as SUM(sales.quantity_sold). | amount_total: total sales amount in that prod × channel × promo × month — derived as SUM(sales.amount_sold).
params.grounded_columns: sales.prod_id | sales.channel_id | sales.promo_id | sales.quantity_sold | sales.amount_sold | sales.time_id | times.time_id | times.calendar_month_desc | times.calendar_year
params.metric: quantity_total = SUM(sales.quantity_sold)  -- aggregated at grain (prod_id, channel_id, promo_id, calendar_month_desc, calendar_year) | amount_total = SUM(sales.amount_sold)  -- aggregated at grain (prod_id, channel_id, promo_id, calendar_month_desc, calendar_year)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to product_current_versions on prod_id — safe because product_current_versions is one-row-per-prod_id (RANK view intends a single current version); joining will not duplicate quantity_total/amount_total. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to currency_monthly_rates on (calendar_year, calendar_month_desc, currency_code) — safe only if currency_monthly_rates is one-row-per-month-per-currency and you filter/align on the same currency; it will not duplicate measures when the rate row is 1:1 with the month used here. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to customer_current_versions or sales_by_customer_demographics only when those views are filtered to one-row-per-customer AND you join at the customer key — BUT this AGG does not contain customer_id; do NOT attempt to join by customer from this view (no customer key present). | do NOT join directly to sales (the raw sales table) or to any other one-to-many detail (for example: product_costs_by_month if it contains multiple cost records per product-month) without re-aggregation — joining a detail with multiple rows per (prod_id, calendar_month_desc, calendar_year) would multiply quantity_total and amount_total. | do NOT join to sibling JOIN views that expand rows into multiple customer/channel/promo combinations (e.g., sales_with_time_product_customer_channel_promo) unless you aggregate the result back to this view's grain — those JOINs are many-to-one or one-to-many relative to this AGG and will duplicate measures. | safe roll-up: you can aggregate this view up (e.g., sum quantity_total/amount_total) to obtain totals by prod_id × calendar_month, by channel_id × calendar_month, by promo_id × calendar_month, or by calendar_month/year — aggregate (SUM) over the grouping columns you drop. | when enriching: if enriching with dimension tables that are truly one-row-per-key (product metadata by prod_id, channel metadata by channel_id, promo metadata by promo_id, time dimension by calendar_month_desc+calendar_year), joins will not duplicate measures. If a dimension can have multiple rows per key, first reduce it to one row per key (e.g., choose current version) before joining.

views.description: Aggregated sales measures rolled up to calendar month and product/channel/promotion. Use for monthly trend analysis and comparisons. Exposes measures quantity_total and amount_total and preserves grouping keys. | Use for: Monthly revenue and volume trends by product/channel/promo; Identify months with largest sales for a product or channel; Feeding time-series models or dashboards

views.name: product_costs_by_month
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  costs.prod_id AS prod_id,
  costs.channel_id AS channel_id,
  costs.promo_id AS promo_id,
  times.calendar_month_desc AS calendar_month_desc,
  times.calendar_year AS calendar_year,
  AVG(unit_cost) AS avg_unit_cost,
  AVG(unit_price) AS avg_unit_price
FROM costs
LEFT JOIN times ON costs.time_id = times.time_id
GROUP BY costs.prod_id, costs.channel_id, costs.promo_id, times.calendar_month_desc, times.calendar_year

params.description: Average unit cost and average unit price per product × channel × promotion × calendar month (year) — month-level cost/price summary.
params.when_to_use: Report average cost and price by product, channel, promotion and calendar month. | Compare cost vs price trends over time for a given product, channel or promotion. | As a month-grain cost/price input when composing higher-level rollups (e.g., product-month, product-year) or joining to sales aggregates (but re-aggregate if joining to many sales rows). | As a cost/price lookup when enriching sales or volume metrics at the same or coarser grain (ensure join keys produce one row per month per product/channel/promo).
params.output_schema: prod_id: Product identifier — derived from costs.prod_id (base column: costs.prod_id) | channel_id: Channel identifier — derived from costs.channel_id (base column: costs.channel_id) | promo_id: Promotion identifier — derived from costs.promo_id (base column: costs.promo_id) | calendar_month_desc: Human-readable month label (e.g., 'Jan 2020') — derived from times.calendar_month_desc (base column: times.calendar_month_desc) | calendar_year: Calendar year (numeric) — derived from times.calendar_year (base column: times.calendar_year) | avg_unit_cost: Average of unit_cost across all cost rows in the grouping — defined as AVG(unit_cost) over the grouping (source values come from costs.unit_cost) | avg_unit_price: Average of unit_price across all cost rows in the grouping — defined as AVG(unit_price) over the grouping (source values come from costs.unit_price)
params.grounded_columns: costs.prod_id | costs.channel_id | costs.promo_id | costs.time_id | costs.unit_cost | costs.unit_price | times.time_id | times.calendar_month_desc | times.calendar_year
params.metric: avg_unit_cost = AVG(costs.unit_cost)  -- average of unit_cost over grouping (prod_id, channel_id, promo_id, calendar_month_desc, calendar_year) | avg_unit_price = AVG(costs.unit_price) -- average of unit_price over same grouping
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension tables that are 1:1 or many-to-1 to this view's grouping keys without re-aggregation. Example: join to a product dimension on prod_id, channel dimension on channel_id, promotion dimension on promo_id, or times dimension on (calendar_month_desc, calendar_year) — safe because product_costs_by_month already has at most one row per (prod_id, channel_id, promo_id, calendar_month_desc, calendar_year), so enriching with attributes will not duplicate measures. | Do NOT directly join product_costs_by_month to any table or view that is one-to-many from the view's grain (would multiply measures) unless you re-aggregate after the join. Examples to avoid or handle with care: |  - Do NOT join directly to sales_with_time_product_customer_channel_promo (JOIN) without aggregation on the sales side or without grouping back to the cost view's grain. sales_with_time_product_customer_channel_promo can have multiple sales rows per (prod_id, channel_id, promo_id, calendar_month), which would duplicate avg_unit_cost/price if joined 1-to-many. |  - Do NOT join directly to sales_by_customer_demographics (JOIN) if that view is at customer or demographic granularity that is many rows per product-month; instead aggregate the demographic/sales side to the product×channel×promo×month grain first. |  - Do NOT join directly to sibling analytic windows/rolling totals like sales_running_total_by_product_month (WIN) unless the running-total view is at the same grain (prod_id × calendar_month) and you account for channel/promo multiplicity; if running total is per product-month only, you must align keys and avoid duplicating per-channel or per-promo rows. | Safe composition patterns: |  - To compute revenue-weighted cost at the same grain, first aggregate sales to (prod_id, channel_id, promo_id, calendar_month_desc, calendar_year) producing sales_qty or sales_amount, then join that aggregated sales result to this view on the full set of keys. After the join you can compute weighted averages or ratios without duplicating rows. |  - To roll up costs to product×month (dropping channel/promo), group this view by prod_id + calendar_month_desc + calendar_year and compute AVG(avg_unit_cost) or a weighted average if you have weights (e.g., sales volume) — note that naive AVG(avg_unit_cost) is unweighted across original cost rows; use weights from an aggregated sales table for correct weighting. |  - Joining to product_current_versions (RANK) is safe if product_current_versions is 1:1 on prod_id; joining to customer_current_versions is unsafe unless you aggregate customers to the product-month grain first. | Rationale: This view's measures are aggregates computed per (prod_id, channel_id, promo_id, calendar_month_desc, calendar_year). Any join that preserves at most one row per that key will not duplicate avg_unit_cost/avg_unit_price. Any join that introduces multiple rows for the same key will multiply those aggregated measures and therefore requires re-aggregation or pre-aggregation of the other side.

views.description: Summarize costs and prices per product per calendar month. Useful to compare cost and price trends or to join with monthly sales for margin calculations. | Use for: Monthly average cost and price per product; Compute gross margin when joined with monthly sales; Track price and cost changes over time

views.name: sales_running_total_by_product_month
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  prod_id AS prod_id,
  calendar_month_desc AS calendar_month_desc,
  calendar_year AS calendar_year,
  amount_total AS amount_total,
  SUM(amount_total) OVER (PARTITION BY prod_id ORDER BY calendar_year, calendar_month_desc ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_amount
FROM (
  SELECT
    prod_id,
    calendar_month_desc,
    calendar_year,
    SUM(amount_sold) AS amount_total
  FROM sales
  LEFT JOIN times ON sales.time_id = times.time_id
  GROUP BY prod_id, calendar_month_desc, calendar_year
)

params.description: Provides per-product monthly sales totals and a cumulative running total of sales (amount) by product across months/years.
params.when_to_use: Show month-by-month sales for a specific product with a running cumulative total | Compare monthly amounts and running totals across products or years | Build reports or visualizations that need a product-level time series with cumulative sums (e.g., YTD running sales by product)
params.output_schema: prod_id: product identifier — derived from sales.prod_id in the underlying sales table | calendar_month_desc: textual month descriptor (e.g., 'Jan', '2023-01' depending on times data) — derived from times.calendar_month_desc | calendar_year: year number for the month row — derived from times.calendar_year | amount_total: aggregated metric SUM(amount_sold) for that prod_id × calendar_month_desc × calendar_year — derived from SUM(sales.amount_sold) grouped by prod_id, calendar_month_desc, calendar_year | running_amount: cumulative running sum of amount_total per prod_id ordered by calendar_year, calendar_month_desc — derived from SUM(amount_total) OVER (PARTITION BY prod_id ORDER BY calendar_year, calendar_month_desc ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
params.grounded_columns: sales.prod_id | sales.amount_sold | sales.time_id | times.time_id | times.calendar_month_desc | times.calendar_year
params.metric: amount_total = SUM(sales.amount_sold) GROUP BY sales.prod_id, times.calendar_month_desc, times.calendar_year | running_amount = SUM(amount_total) OVER (PARTITION BY prod_id ORDER BY calendar_year, calendar_month_desc ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to product_current_versions on prod_id — safe because product_current_versions is a one-row-per-prod_id view (RANK) and will not duplicate this view's month-level rows or measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to times (or other time-dimension views keyed by calendar_month_desc and calendar_year) on calendar_month_desc AND calendar_year — safe when the time dimension is one-row-per-month, it enriches rows without duplication. | do NOT join directly to monthly_sales_agg_by_product_channel_promo or product_costs_by_month without care — those are aggregate-level tables that may be one-row-per-(prod_id, channel, promo, month) or one-row-per-(prod_id, month, cost-version). Joining them without re-aggregation can multiply rows and therefore duplicate amount_total and running_amount. Instead, either: | - pre-aggregate such tables to the same grain (prod_id, calendar_month_desc, calendar_year) and join on prod_id + calendar_month_desc + calendar_year, or | - join on prod_id + calendar_month_desc + calendar_year and then re-aggregate measures (e.g., SUM(amount_total) or recompute running sums) to restore the original grain. | do NOT join to sibling JOIN views that are one-to-many from product (for example sales_with_time_product_customer_channel_promo) without re-aggregating: those joins will create multiple rows per prod_id×month and will therefore multiply amount_total and running_amount. If you need attributes from such joins, first reduce/join to one-row-per-prod_id (e.g., choose latest promo per product-month) or aggregate the joined results back to the (prod_id, calendar_month_desc, calendar_year) grain before using running_amount. | When composing additional metrics: treat amount_total and running_amount as month-grain measures. If you add new dimensions that are many-to-one from this view (for example product attributes that are one-row-per-prod_id), you may join directly on prod_id. If you add dimensions that are many-to-many or many-to-one-to-many, ensure you aggregate back to this view's grain to avoid duplicating measures.

views.description: Running cumulative sales amount within each product across calendar months (ordered by calendar_month_desc). Exposes running_amount so consumers can query cumulative trends and compute month-over-month deltas. Requires a monthly aggregated input (e.g., monthly_sales_agg_by_product_channel_promo or similar). | Use for: Cumulative sales for product over time; Dashboard KPI that shows running totals; Compute share of year-to-date sales by product

views.name: sales_by_customer_demographics
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  sales.prod_id AS prod_id,
  sales.cust_id AS cust_id,
  sales.time_id AS time_id,
  sales.channel_id AS channel_id,
  sales.promo_id AS promo_id,
  sales.quantity_sold AS quantity_sold,
  sales.amount_sold AS amount_sold,
  customers.cust_first_name AS cust_first_name,
  customers.cust_last_name AS cust_last_name,
  customers.cust_year_of_birth AS cust_year_of_birth,
  customers.cust_income_level AS cust_income_level,
  supplementary_demographics.education AS education,
  supplementary_demographics.occupation AS occupation,
  supplementary_demographics.household_size AS household_size,
  supplementary_demographics.affinity_card AS affinity_card,
  supplementary_demographics.cricket AS cricket,
  supplementary_demographics.baseball AS baseball,
  supplementary_demographics.tennis AS tennis,
  supplementary_demographics.soccer AS soccer,
  supplementary_demographics.golf AS golf
FROM sales
LEFT JOIN customers ON sales.cust_id = customers.cust_id
LEFT JOIN supplementary_demographics ON sales.cust_id = supplementary_demographics.cust_id

params.description: Sales facts at the product × customer × time × channel × promo grain enriched with customer demographic attributes (supplementary and core).
params.when_to_use: When you need sales metrics (quantity, amount) scoped to a specific product, customer, time, channel, and promotion and also require customer demographic attributes for filtering, grouping, or reporting. | Composing higher-level aggregates (for example monthly or product-level sales by demographic) by aggregating this view's measures up from its grain. | Joining to single-row dimension views (e.g., canonical product or customer current-version views) to add stable dimensional attributes without duplicating measures.
params.output_schema: prod_id: product identifier from sales.prod_id (base key column). | cust_id: customer identifier from sales.cust_id (base key column). | time_id: time identifier from sales.time_id (base key column). | channel_id: channel identifier from sales.channel_id (base key column). | promo_id: promotion identifier from sales.promo_id (base key column). | quantity_sold: quantity sold measure taken directly from sales.quantity_sold (base metric at the view grain). | amount_sold: sales amount measure taken directly from sales.amount_sold (base metric at the view grain). | cust_first_name: customer's first name from customers.cust_first_name (nullable due to LEFT JOIN). | cust_last_name: customer's last name from customers.cust_last_name (nullable due to LEFT JOIN). | cust_year_of_birth: customer's year of birth from customers.cust_year_of_birth (nullable due to LEFT JOIN). | cust_income_level: customer's income level from customers.cust_income_level (nullable due to LEFT JOIN). | education: supplementary_demographics.education (nullable due to LEFT JOIN). | occupation: supplementary_demographics.occupation (nullable due to LEFT JOIN). | household_size: supplementary_demographics.household_size (nullable due to LEFT JOIN). | affinity_card: supplementary_demographics.affinity_card (nullable due to LEFT JOIN). | cricket: supplementary_demographics.cricket (nullable boolean/flag from supplementary_demographics). | baseball: supplementary_demographics.baseball (nullable boolean/flag from supplementary_demographics). | tennis: supplementary_demographics.tennis (nullable boolean/flag from supplementary_demographics). | soccer: supplementary_demographics.soccer (nullable boolean/flag from supplementary_demographics). | golf: supplementary_demographics.golf (nullable boolean/flag from supplementary_demographics).
params.grounded_columns: sales.prod_id | sales.cust_id | sales.time_id | sales.channel_id | sales.promo_id | sales.quantity_sold | sales.amount_sold | customers.cust_first_name | customers.cust_last_name | customers.cust_year_of_birth | customers.cust_income_level | supplementary_demographics.education | supplementary_demographics.occupation | supplementary_demographics.household_size | supplementary_demographics.affinity_card | supplementary_demographics.cricket | supplementary_demographics.baseball | supplementary_demographics.tennis | supplementary_demographics.soccer | supplementary_demographics.golf
params.metric: quantity_sold = sales.quantity_sold  -- atomic fact measure at the view grain (prod_id, cust_id, time_id, channel_id, promo_id) | amount_sold = sales.amount_sold      -- atomic fact measure at the view grain (prod_id, cust_id, time_id, channel_id, promo_id)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to product_current_versions on prod_id — safe because product_current_versions is a one-row-per-prod_id (RANK canonicalized) so joining will not duplicate this view's measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to customer_current_versions on cust_id — safe because customer_current_versions is a one-row-per-cust_id (RANK canonicalized) so joining will not duplicate this view's measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to currency_monthly_rates on time_id (and currency key if applicable) — safe when currency_monthly_rates is one-row-per-time_id (or per time+currency); ensure you join on the exact key(s) to avoid duplication. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many or aggregate-lacking tables/views such as monthly_sales_agg_by_product_channel_promo or product_costs_by_month without re-aggregation or carefully matching grain — these are aggregated or different-grain views and could cause double-counting or duplication if joined row-for-row. Instead, either (a) aggregate this view up to the target grain (for example SUM(quantity_sold), SUM(amount_sold) grouped by prod_id,time_id,channel_id,promo_id) and then join, or (b) join on keys where the other side is guaranteed to be one-row-per-key. | do NOT join to sibling JOINs that are one-to-many on cust_id (for example any raw contact history or multi-record demographic tables not canonicalized) without first reducing them to one row per cust_id (e.g., via RANK/dedup or aggregation), because the LEFT JOINs in this view already produce at most one supplementary_demographics row per cust_id as written, and joining to additional multi-row sets will multiply measures. | when composing higher-level metrics (monthly, product-level, customer-segment), always aggregate quantity_sold and amount_sold using SUM over the desired grouping keys from this view to preserve correctness (e.g., SUM(amount_sold) GROUP BY prod_id, month(time_id) ...).

views.description: Sales joined to customers and supplementary_demographics (when available) to expose additional demographic flags and attributes per sale. Useful for segmentation and behavioral analysis. Left join preserves sales even if demographic record absent. | Use for: Segment sales by customer interests (sports flags) or demographics; Profile high-value customers with demographic details; Explore purchase patterns by household size or education

views.name: currency_monthly_rates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  country AS country,
  year AS year,
  month AS month,
  to_us AS to_us
FROM currency

params.description: Monthly exchange rate of each country's currency to US (one row per country × year × month).
params.when_to_use: Look up the exchange rate to convert amounts from a country's currency to US for a specific year and month. | Compose monthly currency-normalized monetary measures by joining on country+year+month and applying the to_us rate. | Time-series or monthly-aggregation queries that need a stable, one-row-per-country-month exchange rate.
params.output_schema: country: ISO or internal country identifier for which the rate applies — sourced from currency.country | year: integer calendar year of the rate — sourced from currency.year | month: integer calendar month (1-12) of the rate — sourced from currency.month | to_us: numeric conversion factor (currency → US) for that country/year/month — sourced from currency.to_us
params.metric: to_us = currency.to_us (atomic value; NOT an aggregate in this view)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension or fact tables on country + year + month — safe because currency_monthly_rates has exactly one row per (country, year, month) so joining it to a larger table that has many rows per (country, year, month) will NOT duplicate the currency row but will replicate its single rate onto each matching fact row (this is intended when applying a rate to many transactions). | Do NOT join to another table or view that is one-row-per-country (no year/month) expecting to preserve month granularity without including year+month in the join — omitting year/month will cause unintended many-to-one collapse or duplication relative to time grain. | Do NOT join currency_monthly_rates to another time-grained aggregation that is coarser (e.g., yearly totals) unless you first align grains (e.g., aggregate monthly rates appropriately or aggregate the fact to month before joining) — joining a coarser-table on country only may duplicate/lose temporal semantics. | Safe joins examples: join to monthly_sales_agg_by_product_channel_promo on (country = country AND year = year AND month = month) — safe because this view is one-row-per-country-year-month and its rate will be applied per month per country. | Unsafe join examples: do NOT join to product_current_versions (one row per product) on country — this would multiply/introduce unrelated row-level combinations and is not meaningful without re-aggregation or filtering; likewise avoid joining to sales_running_total_by_product_month without matching (country, year, month) keys unless you intend the multiplication. | If you need to join to a one-to-many table (e.g., customers in a country) but want to preserve aggregate correctness for derived metrics that use to_us, compute the currency-aware measures at the fact/transaction level (apply to_us per row) or re-aggregate after the join; alternatively, pre-aggregate the many-side to the (country, year, month) grain before joining so measures are not artificially multiplied.

views.description: Normalized monthly currency rates with explicit year and month preserved; useful to join to times by calendar_month_desc/year or to sales/cost aggregates to convert amounts to USD. Does not assume specific join keys — left for downstream queries to align by (year, month) or by deriving calendar_month_desc. | Use for: Convert monthly sales or costs into USD using monthly rates; Analyze exchange rate trends by country/month/year
